chunks: Al-Saffar from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother Al-Hussein from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
The waiting period ('iddah) of a woman, when a man enjoys her (in temporary marriage) and then her husband dies, is forty-five days.

So this report is a mistake (wahm) from the narrator, and it is possible that he heard about a temporary marriage whose days had expired, and she was upon it forty-five days, so he attributed it to the one whose husband died.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman in temporary marriage when her husband dies?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi critically analyzes the narration of forty-five days for the 'iddah of temporary marriage (mut'ah) upon the husband's death, attributing it to a narrator's error (wahm) where the fixed term duration was conflated with the waiting period. This reflects the Shia scholarly method of distinguishing between the contractual duration of mut'ah and the post-death waiting period, which generally aligns with the standard four months and ten days unless pregnant. The analysis highlights the precision required in deriving legal rulings from hadith chains in the Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
